title: When Asking for Help, Appeal to People's Self-Interest, Never to Their Mercy or Gratitude
summary: To obtain assistance or favors from others, frame your request around their self-interest and personal benefit rather than relying on mercy or past favors. Most people are pragmatic and motivated by what they stand to gain, making self-interest a far more effective lever than emotional obligation.
example: An elder of a Roman clan begged a warlord for mercy and reminded him of past favors, which burdened the warlord and led to the clan's execution; offering political influence or money would have worked better.
Athens chose to ally with the faction that offered mutual naval strength rather than the faction that appealed to past favors and loyalty.
Japan severed ties with Portuguese traders who pushed religious conversion and instead allied with the Dutch, who focused strictly on trade benefits.
An advisor saved Chinese cities from Genghis Khan by convincing him that preserving the cities and engineers served his strategic and financial interest.
reversal: When dealing with people who want to avoid looking greedy and prefer a noble image, appeal to their desire for public praise, fame, and the appearance of performing a selfless or charitable act.
